the relationships among competitive pressure, organizational innovativeness and organizational structure, and it contributes to our understanding of how organizations respond to environmental and contextual changes.

competitive pressure is positively associated with information intensity, which in turn is positively associated with IT importance, centralization, and formalization.
information intensity is a key factor that links organizational context and structure, and that competitive pressure and innovational innovativeness have a positive effect on information intensity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of this study suggest that the IP perspective provides a useful framework for understanding the relationships among environmental and organizational variables.

competitive pressure is positively related to information intensity and IT importance, which in turn are positively related to centralization and formal structure, and that innovativeness is positively related to IT importance and formalization, which in turn is positively related to centralizaton.

the IP view of organizations provides a useful theoretical framework and a promising research approach to the investigation of the relationships among organizational contextual variables, IP-related variables, and organizational structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that

information intensity is a key variable that helps to explain the effects of environmental and contextual variables, as well as the relationships of these environmental and contextual variables among themselves and to structure.
, in order to better understand the relationship between organizational structure and context, we should focus on information-processing activities.
